I am against eugenics, simply because I think our understanding of intelligence is woefully short-sighted. I hate to sound like a SJW here, but I really do believe that people that have shortcomings in one area are often gifted in another. For instance, I know a number of people that are technology-averse...yet they tend to be reliable, trustworthy friends. In short, I believe that there are many types of intelligence, and taken as a whole, they help us to balance out society and find the truth.

As far as cloning goes, I really don't know. Should someone be able to store their own DNA? Of course. In fact, I think that everyone should have exclusive rights to their own DNA by default. Should people be able to clone themselves for the purpose of harvesting organs for transplant? I wouldn't be for that at all. Maybe once they can clone a body with nothing more than a brain stem to carry on basic functions, but other than that, no way.

Gene editing? It's coming whether we like it or not, so no point in stopping it. But I see much malignancy and folly on the path to knowledge in those arts. Again, I think people tend to trivialize the complexity of things, which leads to unintended consequences. Editing one innocuous gene might give your child a larger penis, but maybe that was an evolutionary step that helped us to avoid some dreaded penis wasting disease that lurks in the soil.

Oh, and some advice: read each and every detail of a company's privacy policy before having anything to do with handing over your DNA. There used to be one group that pledged to destroy your DNA and all associated information at your request (it was a university). That group is no longer around, so far as I can tell. Besides that, every company that I've looked at retains the right to sell your information. Bear in mind that it's not just yours--you will be giving away details on all of your blood relations as well. There have already been stories about subpoena's being placed for the DNA of people who are related to someone suspected of committing a crime.

That having been said, they can grab your DNA from your trash any time they wish (in the USA at least), so if ever there is a company that offers to actually -pay- for your DNA info, I'd consider it.
